claim: The BOM identifies ABC-123 as a NEMA 17 stepper motor with quantity 2 and row ID 3.
The source lists mass as 0.280 kg per motor.
The source describes the function as controlled rotary actuation for a motion axis.
The source lists likely materials including steel, copper, aluminum, permanent magnets, bearings, polymer insulation, and connector.
The source gives the manufacturing route: stamp laminations, wind coils, assemble rotor and shaft, install bearings, assemble housing, wire connector, and test electrically.
BOM row 4 identifies AL-2040 as four units of 2040 aluminum extrusion rail used as machine frame rail.
Mass is 0.55 kg per 1 m rail.
Function is structural frame member.
Likely materials are 6061 or 6063 aluminum alloy with a minor anodized oxide layer.
Manufacturing route is billet casting, homogenizing, hot extrusion, straightening, age hardening, cutting, and optional anodizing.
The BOM identifies BRG-608 as a 608ZZ radial ball bearing with quantity 6 and row ID 6.
The source lists one bearing at 0.012 kg.
The source describes the function as supporting rotating shafts and idlers with low friction.
The source lists likely materials including chrome steel rings and balls, steel shields, polymer or steel cage, and trace lubricant.
The source describes manufacturing steps including blank forming, turning, heat treatment, grinding, ball manufacture, assembly, shield installation, lubrication, and inspection.
BOM row 7 identifies GT2-200 as two units of GT2 timing belt 200 mm loop for the axis belt drive.
One 200 mm closed-loop belt has mass 0.018 kg.
The belt transmits motion from pulley to axis carriage.
Likely materials include neoprene or polyurethane body, fiberglass or steel tensile cords, and tooth facing fabric.
Manufacturing uses cord reinforcement, molded or extruded toothed belt body, elastomer curing, loop cutting, and tooth pitch inspection.
The BOM identifies M3x12 as an M3 stainless socket screw with row IDs 1 and 2 and total quantity 20.
The source estimates one M3 x 12 stainless socket screw at 0.0012 kg.
The source describes the function as reusable frame and bracket fastening.
The source lists likely material as a stainless steel body with negligible surface finish mass.
The source lists the manufacturing route as cold heading, thread rolling, socket forming, passivation, and inspection.
BOM row 11 identifies PLATE-3MM as two units of 3 mm aluminum mounting plate for motor and electronics mounting.
One mounting plate is estimated at 0.180 kg.
The plate provides a flat mounting surface for motors and electronics.
Likely materials are aluminum alloy plate with optional oxide surface.
Manufacturing route is rolling sheet or plate, cutting blank, drilling mounting holes, deburring, optional anodizing, and dimensional inspection.
The BOM identifies PSU-24V as a 24 V DC power supply module with quantity 1 and row ID 9.
The source lists mass as 0.220 kg.
The source describes the function as converting input power to regulated 24 V DC for motors and electronics.
The source lists likely materials including FR-4 PCB, copper, ferrite cores, aluminum heat sink, steel enclosure, capacitors, semiconductors, solder, and polymers.
The source lists manufacturing steps including PCB fabrication, magnetic component winding, SMT/THT assembly, enclosure fabrication, electrical safety testing, burn-in, and final inspection.
BOM row 8 identifies PUL-20T as four units of GT2 20 tooth aluminum pulley used as motor and idler pulleys.
One pulley has mass 0.010 kg.
The pulley couples motor shaft or idler shaft to GT2 belt motion.
Likely materials are aluminum alloy body and small steel set screws.
Manufacturing route is turning an aluminum blank, machining timing teeth, drilling and tapping set-screw holes, deburring, optional anodizing, and bore and pitch inspection.
The BOM identifies SENS-9 as an optical endstop sensor board with quantity 3 and row ID 5.
The source lists board mass as 0.006 kg.
The source describes the function as detecting axis home position.
The source lists likely materials including FR-4 glass-epoxy PCB, copper traces, solder, small ICs, photointerrupter package, connector, and polymer bodies.
The source lists the manufacturing route as PCB fabrication, solder mask and finish, SMT/THT placement, reflow or wave soldering, and optical/electrical test.
BOM row 10 identifies WIRE-22 as 5 m of 22 AWG stranded hook-up wire used for a low-voltage wiring harness.
Mass is 0.008 kg per meter.
The wire carries low-voltage power and signals between electronics and sensors.
Likely materials are stranded copper conductor and PVC or silicone insulation.
Manufacturing route is copper wire drawing, conductor stranding, insulation extrusion, cooling, marking, spooling, and electrical testing.
